notes.title: Ascendancies
notes.summary: A subclass charm, the Ascendancy Stone, unlocked by five Hell superuniques and upgraded through five endgame challenges.

children.value: is a subclass granted by an Ascendancy Stone, a charm with its own skills and bonuses. To get one, kill the five special superuniques on Hell (Acts 1 to 3 have one each, Act 5 has two), cube their elemental orbs into an Orb of Creation, then cube the orb with Blemished gems; the colours pick the ascendancy (
Each later tier is a challenge finished in the cube: Nihlathak on Hell, all three Uber Tristram bosses within a minute, Primordial Soulstones from map bosses, and a tier 5 map boss (
). Tiers can be done in any order.
You can wear one stone at a time. It cannot be moved to another character, corrupted or anointed, and after a death you must re-equip it (

notes.title: Cube basics
notes.summary: How ESR uses the Horadric Cube, how to read the official recipe page, and the rules that make a recipe silently fail.

children.value: In ESR almost every upgrade is a cube recipe. The official Cube Recipes page is the full reference: sections of short rules followed by Input → Output tables. It is not a tutorial, so here is how to read it.
"Any …" means any item of that kind. "Torso" is body armor, "Armor" is every kind of armor.
"ilvl = char level" and similar lines give the output's item level, which decides the affixes it can roll.
Underlined materials in an output are handed back to you; removing a Forging, for example, returns its Anvil Stones.
Keys, Scrolls of Identify, Antidote Potions and the like often act as switches that pick which variant of a recipe runs.
most recipes that reroll the input ignore items with a Forging; remove it first (

items cannot be changed by any recipe.
older guides warn that more than 100 items can crash the game (
Since 3.2.11 the transmute hotkey (set it under Options > Controls) works with the cube closed, and holding it repeats.
Material tabs in the stash upgrade with Shift + click and downgrade with Alt + click, no cube needed.

notes.summary: Respecs are counted but can be refilled, dying in map boss areas costs no experience, and most gear choices can be undone.

children.value: Hold Alt and click any of the + buttons on the character screen to reset every stat and skill point. Each use spends one respec from a counter shown in that button's tooltip. A new character starts with a few; characters created before the counter existed start with none. The Introductory Book still calls respecs free, which predates the counter.

notes.title: D-stoning, gem melding and Mapling
notes.summary: Permanent stat boosts that raise an item's level requirement, and Secret Recipe 50 to lower it again so you can keep going.

children.value: cubes an item with one of the Dragon Stone forms, sometimes with a Key or potion as a switch, to add a small permanent stat (

the stat reaches its D-stoning cap, which counts only what D-stoning added (enhanced damage and defense can never pass 500% in total), or
the item's level requirement penalty reaches the fail-safe limit for its tier (normal and jewelry allow the most, elite the least).

notes.title: Glossary
notes.summary: Short definitions of the ESR words used in this guide, each linked to the note that explains it.

children.value: New to the jargon? Each term links to the note that explains it;

entries.definition: A drop that names one vanilla (LoD) unique; matching coupons, alone or with Wild Cards, cube into that unique.
A common material that identifies Ancient Scrolls and feeds many recipes; eight make a Dragon Stone.
A numbered scroll (1 to 50) that unlocks the Secret Recipe with the same number; it is returned after each use.
A random bonus added with an Orb of Anointment (gear) or the three Demonic organs of the Prime Evils (unique charms); it cannot brick the item.
A stronger crafting stone made from Dragon Stones and a Perfect Gem; the main cost of Skill and Stat Forging.
A subclass specialisation granted by an Ascendancy Stone, upgraded through five tiers of challenges.
An ESR gem grade between Flawless and Perfect, used for rare rerolls, socketing exceptional items and Ascendancy Stones.
A modifier added by Inarius' Everburning Halo; a Branded item can no longer be changed by any recipe.
A unique large charm that the official cube page lists in the Starter Pack; the 3.2.12 game files give no way to get one.
A cube recipe that turns a magic item, a class's Dragon Stone form, a Perfect Gem and a jewel into crafted gear with that class's skills.
Cubing an item with a Worldstone Shard for a random strong bonus, with a chance to turn the item into a random rare.
Cubing several coupons of one tier with a Randomizing Stone to get a random coupon.
One of twelve ESR socketable minerals (such as Frozen Soul or Pulsing Opal) in Chipped, Flawed and normal grades.
Cubing an item with a Dragon Stone form to add a small permanent stat at the cost of a higher level requirement.
A drop that, cubed with the ES rune of the same number, becomes the vanilla rune of that number.
The main crafting stone of ESR, used for D-stoning, class crafts, many Secret Recipes and Anvil Stones.
The shapes a Dragon Stone cycles through when cubed alone (Holy Symbol, Blackmoor, Forging Hammer, Crushed Gem, Spider's Silk, Tyranium Ore, Void Shard); each is a different ingredient.
A consumable item that, transmuted alone in Act 5 Hell, opens a high-level zone with a boss; maps come in five tiers.
ESR's own rune line, named after Japanese syllables from I up to Wo; used in ESR runewords, Rune Forging and many recipes.
A cube recipe that adds one extra, removable bonus to an item; an item holds one Forging at a time.
Cubing an item with a Perfect Gem and Decipherers to add that gem's chipped bonus permanently, raising the level requirement.
A runeword-like recipe that uses gems instead of runes in a socketed white item.
One of ESR's top socketables (Moon, Fire, Water up to God), made from a Null Rune and crystals.
A book from the Starter Pack that counts kills and takes permanent bonuses at kill milestones and after endgame boss kills.
A vanilla rune (El to Zod), built from a Decal and an ES rune; used in the reworked vanilla runewords.
A material made mainly from spare unique charms; spent on Mapling, All Skill Forging and several high-end recipes.
Secret Recipe 50, which spends a Maple Leaf and a Sa Rune to lower an item's level requirement penalty so it can be D-stoned again.
A cube recipe that gives a weapon or armor a bonus package only a mercenary can use; three Antidote Potions undo it.
The general stocker for organs, Dragon Stones, Decipherers, coupons, Maple Leaves and more; also turns spare set and unique gear into Decipherer points.
A top-tier unique that only drops in Endgame Maps, some of them from one specific boss.
The one-socket charm from the Starter Pack; Secret Recipe 49 turns it into a Veteran's Odd Charm.
A rune made from a Wo Rune and a Full Rejuvenation Potion; the base for every Kanji rune.
Monster parts (Hearts, Souls, Brains, Eyes, Scalps, Horns, Fangs, Jawbones, Spleens, Quills, Tails) used for tinkering, the Vessel of Souls and conversions.
A skill granted by an item that any class can use, such as the elemental Surges and Brands.
A stocker for rings, amulets, jewels, charms and quivers that stores them as points by rarity and rerolls them into new ones.
Using Lucion's Relic of Sanctification on a jewel for a one-time bonus that cannot be undone.
One of the numbered cube recipes that only work with the matching identified Ancient Scroll in the cube.
The cube ingredient that adds sockets to an item, together with gems whose grade matches the item tier.
A container item that destroys the materials you cube into it and stores them as points you can take out later.
An area currently terrorized, with stronger monsters; terrorized champions and uniques can drop Worldstone Shards, and level 96 ones can drop Endgame Maps.
A potion used, three at a time, to remove a Forging from an item; it also appears in key and charm recipes.
Cubing gear with organs to add small permanent bonuses, limited by hidden tinkering points on each item.
A consumable made from Dragon Stones; right-click it to add one respec to the character's respec counter.
A mythical amulet that you feed organs in the cube to build up bonuses, then turn into a mythical weapon; it is not meant to be worn.
A removable specialisation applied to a class weapon with an awakened Weapon Mastery Token; it changes how skills work with that weapon.
A joker made from spare coupons that replaces the third matching coupon in unique recipes and appears in several gem recipes.

notes.title: Surviving Hell
notes.summary: Hell brings heavy resistance and leech penalties and tougher monsters. What to prepare before you leave Nightmare.

children.value: ESR's campaign is harder than vanilla, and the jump from late Nightmare into Hell is the steepest part. These are the difficulty penalties straight from the game files:
In short: your resistances drop sharply, life and mana leech become much weaker, monsters get extra skill levels, and freeze, chill and curse durations on them shrink.
get fire, cold, lightning and poison back to the cap after the penalty, and add some physical and magic resistance if you can.
Stat Forging with a chipped Topaz adds % maximum life (
); the first Kill Ledger milestones add resistances and more (

Skill Forging (+1 to your class skills) on every slot is the standard early boost for skill-based builds. Plan a way past immunities, such as Lower Resist charges, a Conviction aura forged onto your amulet with a White Aura Stone, or a Hell Combat Desert Mercenary, whose skills include Conviction (
farm Nightmare's special areas first. The official Maps page lists them (the Secret Cow Level, Blood Raven's Workshop, Lost Farm and others) and recommends them once you have beaten that difficulty.
raise it for more experience and drops when you are comfortable, and lower it when you are not.
ESR changes several maps and moves some quest areas; a few vanilla zones are now dangerous special areas. Check the official Maps page when a quest area is not where you expect.

notes.title: Start here
notes.summary: What changes when you come to ESR from vanilla D2R, and how to use this guide.

children.value: Eastern Sun Resurrected (ESR) is a total conversion of Diablo II Resurrected by CelestialRayOne. If you know vanilla D2R, these are the five things that will surprise you:
Most items are new or reworked.
s, coupon-made vanilla uniques and mythical uniques. Vanilla runewords still exist, but their runes are built from parts (
The Horadric Cube is your main tool.
Hundreds of recipes reroll, upgrade and enhance gear. Read
Organs, Dragon Stones, coupons and scrolls drop all the time;
s keep them as points instead of stash space (
Monsters and skills are rebalanced, and the step from Nightmare into Hell is steep (
Endgame Maps, Ascendancies, Diablo Clone and Uber Tristram are reworked (

The five steps above follow a first character from town to the endgame. Read them in order the first time; every note is short, lists what to know first, and points to the next one. Before you leave the Rogue Encampment, read
When you pick up something strange, use the "I found something" row or

notes.title: Tinkering
notes.summary: Cube organs into gear for small permanent bonuses until the item's hidden tinkering points run out.

notes.title: Vessel of Souls

glossary.definition: A container item that destroys the materials you cube into it and stores them as points you can take out later.
The general stocker for organs, Dragon Stones, Decipherers, coupons, Maple Leaves and more; also turns spare set and unique gear into Decipherer points.
A stocker for rings, amulets, jewels, charms and quivers that stores them as points by rarity and rerolls them into new ones.
A drop that names one vanilla (LoD) unique; matching coupons, alone or with Wild Cards, cube into that unique.
A joker made from spare coupons that replaces the third matching coupon in unique recipes and appears in several gem recipes.
Cubing several coupons of one tier with a Randomizing Stone to get a random coupon.
A numbered scroll (1 to 50) that unlocks the Secret Recipe with the same number; it is returned after each use.
A common material that identifies Ancient Scrolls and feeds many recipes; eight make a Dragon Stone.
One of the numbered cube recipes that only work with the matching identified Ancient Scroll in the cube.
The main crafting stone of ESR, used for D-stoning, class crafts, many Secret Recipes and Anvil Stones.
The shapes a Dragon Stone cycles through when cubed alone (Holy Symbol, Blackmoor, Forging Hammer, Crushed Gem, Spider's Silk, Tyranium Ore, Void Shard); each is a different ingredient.
A stronger crafting stone made from Dragon Stones and a Perfect Gem; the main cost of Skill and Stat Forging.
A cube recipe that adds one extra, removable bonus to an item; an item holds one Forging at a time.
A potion used, three at a time, to remove a Forging from an item; it also appears in key and charm recipes.
Cubing an item with a Dragon Stone form to add a small permanent stat at the cost of a higher level requirement.
Cubing an item with a Perfect Gem and Decipherers to add that gem's chipped bonus permanently, raising the level requirement.
A material made mainly from spare unique charms; spent on Mapling, All Skill Forging and several high-end recipes.
Secret Recipe 50, which spends a Maple Leaf and a Sa Rune to lower an item's level requirement penalty so it can be D-stoned again.
Cubing gear with organs to add small permanent bonuses, limited by hidden tinkering points on each item.
Cubing an item with a Worldstone Shard for a random strong bonus, with a chance to turn the item into a random rare.
A random bonus added with an Orb of Anointment (gear) or the three Demonic organs of the Prime Evils (unique charms); it cannot brick the item.
Using Lucion's Relic of Sanctification on a jewel for a one-time bonus that cannot be undone.
A modifier added by Inarius' Everburning Halo; a Branded item can no longer be changed by any recipe.
An ESR gem grade between Flawless and Perfect, used for rare rerolls, socketing exceptional items and Ascendancy Stones.
One of twelve ESR socketable minerals (such as Frozen Soul or Pulsing Opal) in Chipped, Flawed and normal grades.
Monster parts (Hearts, Souls, Brains, Eyes, Scalps, Horns, Fangs, Jawbones, Spleens, Quills, Tails) used for tinkering, the Vessel of Souls and conversions.
ESR's own rune line, named after Japanese syllables from I up to Wo; used in ESR runewords, Rune Forging and many recipes.
A drop that, cubed with the ES rune of the same number, becomes the vanilla rune of that number.
A vanilla rune (El to Zod), built from a Decal and an ES rune; used in the reworked vanilla runewords.
A rune made from a Wo Rune and a Full Rejuvenation Potion; the base for every Kanji rune.
One of ESR's top socketables (Moon, Fire, Water up to God), made from a Null Rune and crystals.
A runeword-like recipe that uses gems instead of runes in a socketed white item.
The cube ingredient that adds sockets to an item, together with gems whose grade matches the item tier.
A unique large charm that the official cube page lists in the Starter Pack; the 3.2.12 game files give no way to get one.
The one-socket charm from the Starter Pack; Secret Recipe 49 turns it into a Veteran's Odd Charm.
A book from the Starter Pack that counts kills and takes permanent bonuses at kill milestones and after endgame boss kills.
An area currently terrorized, with stronger monsters; terrorized champions and uniques can drop Worldstone Shards, and level 96 ones can drop Endgame Maps.
A consumable item that, transmuted alone in Act 5 Hell, opens a high-level zone with a boss; maps come in five tiers.
A subclass specialisation granted by an Ascendancy Stone, upgraded through five tiers of challenges.
A mythical amulet that you feed organs in the cube to build up bonuses, then turn into a mythical weapon; it is not meant to be worn.
A consumable made from Dragon Stones; right-click it to add one respec to the character's respec counter.
A top-tier unique that only drops in Endgame Maps, some of them from one specific boss.
A removable specialisation applied to a class weapon with an awakened Weapon Mastery Token; it changes how skills work with that weapon.
A cube recipe that gives a weapon or armor a bonus package only a mercenary can use; three Antidote Potions undo it.
A skill granted by an item that any class can use, such as the elemental Surges and Brands.
A cube recipe that turns a magic item, a class's Dragon Stone form, a Perfect Gem and a jewel into crafted gear with that class's skills.
